annual_compliance: Annual return each year in the allocated month, signed by a director (none in the incorporation year); the Registrar must strike the company off if a return is not filed within 6 months.

Annual return each year in the allocated month (none in the incorporation year); accounts must be audited (fine up to $4,000); the Registrar must strike the company off if a return is not filed within 6 months.

No broad annual accounts-filing regime is published for associations under the Corporations Act 1972; IBCs pay only an annual fee with no accounts, so ongoing compliance is minimal and largely unpublished.

Annual return signed by a director within 42 days after the AGM, with certified balance sheet, P&L, auditors' and directors' reports; no strike-off provision, so non-filing is a criminal offence for company and officers.
No accounts-filing duty; failing to pay the annual fee or keep a registered agent lapses after a year, then 90 days' notice, then proclamation revokes the articles and dissolves the entity.
Annual report to the Secretary of Finance and Administration with a $5 fee; initial report within 60 days; reports are made public. No audit threshold or strike-off deadline is published.

Annual activity and income/expense statement to the provincial governorate by end of April (foreign associations by end of February); non-filing draws administrative fines and persistent breach can lead to dissolution.

To keep the income-tax exemption the charity must stay registered with the Revenue Service and file annual reports with program information and audited financial statements; no strike-off deadline is published.
Charities file an annual activity report to the Governmental Commission; audit is mandatory above 5,000,000 AMD (raised to 10,000,000 AMD); CSOs receiving public resources must report openly.

Annual financial reports to the Ministry of Justice are due by 1 April; the 2000 NGOs Law also requires notifying changes; non-compliance exposes the NGO to administrative penalties; strike-off deadline unpublished.
Even tax-exempt NPOs must file income tax returns and comply with state reporting and re-reporting under the Tax Code; no charity-specific annual deadline or strike-off consequence is published.

Tax-exempt non-commercial organizations must still file income tax returns and audited accounts under the Tax Code; entrepreneurial income is taxable; no charity-specific deadline or strike-off rule published.

Associations register with the Ministry of Justice (Turkmen-citizen founders, registration fee); no annual report deadline, audit threshold or strike-off consequence is clearly published under the 2014 law.

All public associations file income tax returns, audited accounts and grant-receipt reports; since 2019 detailed financial reports must also be posted on their websites; penalties apply, strike-off unpublished.

Tax-exempt NCOs must still file returns and report revenue and property to state bodies; charities make annual reports open to the media, and fund-raisers publish an annual report of amounts collected and used.

Every registered NGO files an annual report of activities and financial operations to the supervising board, may be ordered to submit periodic reports, and must produce records for inspection at the board's request.

Associations file a tax return within 3 months of fiscal year-end with OHADA accounting documents; foreign and religious ONGs need Interior authorisation, local non-religious ones declare; no audit threshold.

ONGs file an annual activity programme by the last working day of November and, 3 months after year-end, an execution report with financial statements; sanctions: 3-month notice, suspension, withdrawal of ONG status.

Associations register under the 1962 ordinance and must report any change of administration, direction or bylaws to the State within 30 days; the tax administration also requires a report disclosing payments made.

NGOs declared under the 1901-style law follow corporate rules: annual tax return plus CEMAC/OHADA accounting forms; no NGO-specific reporting beyond corporate returns; no strike-off deadline published.
